claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is equiatomic.
HfNbTaTiZr can exist as a metastable single beta-BCC matrix.
The initial beta-BCC state is a random solid solution.
The random HfNbTaTiZr state has severe lattice distortion caused by atomic-size mismatch and random chemical distribution.
Monte Carlo-based equilibration can generate varying degrees of chemical short-range order.
In HfNbTaTiZr, induced SRO nucleates HfTi and TiZr binary clusters that undergo a percolative transition into B2-like structures.
There is an intermediate-temperature regime in which SRO is stable while long-range ordering is not dominant.
A single-phase BCC matrix is required to observe the proposed percolative transition.
The structural mediator is a spanning network of ordered HfTi and TiZr B2-like clusters embedded in the BCC matrix.
Formation of ordered B2-like clusters lowers local atomic displacement amplitudes and lattice distortion relative to the random alloy.
Reduced local lattice distortion decreases the scattering of high-frequency phonons.
A percolating network of ordered clusters provides continuous low-scattering, high-conductivity pathways for phonons.
The combined reduction in distortion and formation of percolative pathways can increase lattice thermal conductivity relative to the random solid solution.
Random solid-solution HfNbTaTiZr has low thermal conductivity because severe lattice distortion and random chemical arrangements strongly scatter phonons.
A conductivity increase occurs only after the ordered SRO clusters form a material-spanning network.
If the ordered clusters remain isolated, scattering at their boundaries causes conductivity to decrease.
Percolative ordering should be accompanied by lower atomic displacement amplitudes and sharper high-frequency phonon-DOS features.
Comparing displacement amplitudes, high-frequency phonon DOS, and thermal conductivity before and after ordering provides a falsification test against the random-alloy baseline.
